fixed.q: The "Zone of Proximal Development" was proposed by:
fixed.w: ZPD is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what they can do with help. Help from a teacher or peer within the ZPD is called scaffolding.

fixed.q: Temporary support given to a learner that is gradually withdrawn is called:
fixed.w: The term comes from Wood, Bruner and Ross and is linked to Vygotsky's ZPD.

fixed.q: Operant conditioning is associated with:
fixed.w: Skinner: operant conditioning with reinforcement. Pavlov: classical conditioning. Thorndike: trial and error and the laws of learning. Bandura: social/observational learning.

fixed.q: Classical conditioning was demonstrated by Ivan Pavlov using:
fixed.w: Pavlov paired a bell (conditioned stimulus) with food until the bell alone caused salivation.

fixed.q: Thorndike's laws of learning are:
o: Law of readiness, law of exercise and law of effect
fixed.w: Thorndike (trial-and-error learning) gave the laws of readiness, exercise and effect, based on cat-in-puzzle-box experiments.

fixed.q: Learning by observing and imitating a model was emphasised by:
fixed.w: Bandura's social learning theory (Bobo doll experiment): attention, retention, reproduction and motivation.

fixed.q: Insight learning was demonstrated by:
fixed.w: Köhler (Gestalt school) studied chimpanzees (Sultan) who solved problems suddenly by insight.

fixed.q: In constructivism, learners:
o: Build their own understanding through experience
Passively receive knowledge from the teacher
Learn only through rewards and punishment
fixed.w: Constructivism (Piaget, Vygotsky, Bruner) sees the learner as an active builder of knowledge.

fixed.q: Discovery learning is associated with:
fixed.w: Bruner promoted discovery learning, the spiral curriculum and three modes of representation: enactive, iconic and symbolic.

fixed.q: Theory of Multiple Intelligences was given by:
fixed.w: Gardner (1983) listed linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, musical, bodily-kinaesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal and naturalistic intelligences.

fixed.q: According to Piaget, a child in the concrete operational stage is aged about:
fixed.w: Piaget's stages: sensorimotor (0–2), pre-operational (2–7), concrete operational (7–11), formal operational (11+).

fixed.q: Abstract and hypothetical reasoning develops in Piaget's:
fixed.w: Formal operational (11+): abstract thinking and hypothetico-deductive reasoning, suitable for programming logic.

fixed.q: Fitting new information into existing mental schemas is called:
fixed.w: Assimilation fits new information into existing schemas. Accommodation changes the schemas.

fixed.q: Stages of moral development were proposed by:
fixed.w: Kohlberg: three levels (pre-conventional, conventional, post-conventional) with six stages.

fixed.q: Inclusive education means:
o: Educating children with diverse needs, including disabilities, together in regular classrooms
Separate schools for children with disabilities
fixed.w: Inclusion places all learners in the same classroom with suitable support. The RPwD Act 2016 supports it.

fixed.q: A learning disability affecting reading is called:
fixed.w: Dyslexia: reading. Dysgraphia: writing. Dyscalculia: mathematics. Dyspraxia: motor coordination.

fixed.q: Maslow's highest level of need is:
fixed.w: Maslow's hierarchy from the bottom: physiological, safety, love and belonging, esteem, self-actualisation.

fixed.q: The project method of teaching was developed by:
fixed.w: Kilpatrick developed the project method on the basis of Dewey's pragmatism (learning by doing).

fixed.q: Moving from specific examples to a general rule is the:
fixed.w: Inductive: examples → rule (good for understanding). Deductive: rule → examples (faster).

fixed.q: The maxim that teaching should proceed from the known to the:
fixed.w: Common maxims: known to unknown, simple to complex, concrete to abstract, particular to general, whole to part, easy to difficult.

fixed.q: "Learning by doing" was emphasised by:
fixed.w: Dewey (pragmatism) stressed experience and activity-based learning.

fixed.q: For teaching how to write and run a program, the most suitable method is:
o: Demonstration followed by hands-on lab practice
fixed.w: Programming is a skill; it is learnt best by watching a demonstration and then practising in the lab.

fixed.q: Breaking a large problem into smaller sub-problems while teaching programming encourages:
fixed.w: Computational thinking: decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithm design.

fixed.q: Brainstorming as a teaching technique mainly develops:
fixed.w: Brainstorming (Alex Osborn) generates many ideas without judging them first.

fixed.q: In a flipped classroom:
o: Students study content at home and do activities in class
The teacher lectures more in class
fixed.w: Flipped learning moves instruction (videos, readings) home and uses class time for practice and discussion.

fixed.q: Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience places at its base:
fixed.w: Dale's cone goes from concrete (direct experience) at the base to abstract (verbal symbols) at the top.

fixed.q: The revised Bloom's taxonomy (2001) places at the highest level:
fixed.w: Revised order: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create (Anderson and Krathwohl).

fixed.q: In the original Bloom's taxonomy (1956), the lowest level of the cognitive domain is:
fixed.w: Original: Knowledge, Comprehension, Application, Analysis, Synthesis, Evaluation.

fixed.q: Bloom's taxonomy has three domains:
fixed.w: Cognitive (thinking), affective (feelings and attitudes) and psychomotor (physical skills).

fixed.q: "Students will be able to write a C program to find the largest of three numbers" is an objective at the level of:
fixed.w: Using learnt concepts to produce a solution in a new situation is application.

fixed.q: Herbart's five formal steps of lesson planning begin with:
fixed.w: Herbart: Preparation, Presentation, Comparison/Association, Generalisation, Application (Recapitulation is often added).

fixed.q: Micro-teaching was developed at:
fixed.w: Micro-teaching was developed at Stanford (Dwight Allen and colleagues, 1963).

fixed.q: A standard micro-teaching cycle in India lasts:
fixed.w: Teach 6 + feedback 6 + re-plan 12 + re-teach 6 + re-feedback 6 = 36 minutes.

fixed.q: The first step of any lesson plan is to decide the:
fixed.w: Objectives decide the content, method, activities and evaluation.

fixed.q: Assessment carried out during teaching to improve learning is:
fixed.w: Formative = assessment for learning, ongoing. Summative = assessment of learning, at the end.

fixed.q: A test that identifies a learner's specific weaknesses and learning difficulties is a:
fixed.w: A diagnostic test finds the cause of difficulty, which is followed by remedial teaching.

fixed.q: The consistency of a test's results is its:
fixed.w: Reliability: consistency of scores. Validity: does it measure what it claims to measure.

fixed.q: A test measures what it is intended to measure. This quality is:
fixed.w: A test can be reliable but not valid; a valid test must be reliable.

fixed.q: CCE stands for:
fixed.w: CCE covered scholastic and co-scholastic areas through regular formative and summative assessment (RTE Act 2009).

fixed.q: A blueprint of a question paper shows:
o: Weightage of content, objectives and question types
Only the marks of each student
fixed.w: The blueprint is a 3-D chart of content areas × objectives × types of questions.

fixed.q: A rubric is:
o: A scoring guide with criteria and performance levels
fixed.w: Rubrics make the scoring of projects and programs transparent and consistent.

fixed.q: Evaluating a student against a fixed standard rather than against other students is:
fixed.w: Criterion-referenced: has the learner reached the standard? Norm-referenced: rank compared with the group.

fixed.q: A record of a student's work collected over time to show progress is a:
fixed.w: A portfolio collects selected work (programs, projects) showing growth.

fixed.q: NEP 2020 replaces the 10+2 structure with:
fixed.w: Foundational (3–8 yrs), Preparatory (8–11), Middle (11–14), Secondary (14–18).

fixed.q: According to NEP 2020, coding is to be introduced from:
fixed.w: NEP 2020 recommends coding from the middle stage, i.e. Class 6.

fixed.q: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009 covers children aged:
fixed.w: RTE 2009 (in force 1 April 2010) applies to ages 6–14. Article 21A was added by the 86th Amendment (2002).

fixed.q: Under RTE Section 12(1)(c), private unaided schools must reserve, for disadvantaged and weaker sections:
fixed.w: 25% of seats at entry level (Class 1 or pre-primary) are reserved for EWS and disadvantaged groups.

fixed.q: The National Curriculum Framework 2005 was prepared by:
fixed.w: NCERT prepared NCF 2005 (chaired by Prof. Yash Pal), stressing linking knowledge to life outside school and learning without burden.

fixed.q: Which is the Government of India's MOOC platform for online courses?
fixed.w: SWAYAM offers MOOCs from school to PG level. DIKSHA is a platform for teachers and school content. NROER is an open educational resources repository.

fixed.q: DIKSHA platform is mainly meant for:
fixed.w: DIKSHA (2017) gives energised textbooks (QR codes), teacher training and school learning content.

fixed.q: Using computer programs to deliver instruction, drill and practice is called:
fixed.w: CAI includes tutorials, drill and practice, simulations and games.

fixed.q: Blended learning means:
o: Combining face-to-face teaching with online learning
fixed.w: Blended learning mixes classroom instruction with digital and online media.

fixed.q: For teaching a sorting algorithm, the best teaching aid is:
o: An animation or simulation showing each step
fixed.w: Visualising each comparison and swap makes an abstract algorithm concrete.

fixed.q: Teaching Boolean logic gates in Class 11 is most effective with:
o: Truth tables plus a simulator or circuit activity
fixed.w: Learners connect the symbol, the truth table and real behaviour through activity.

fixed.q: When students write code with a partner, one typing and one reviewing, it is called:
fixed.w: Pair programming (driver and navigator), from agile practice, improves learning and code quality.

fixed.q: Flanders' Interaction Analysis Category System has how many categories?
fixed.w: Flanders' FIACS: 10 categories (7 teacher talk, 2 student talk, 1 silence or confusion).

fixed.q: Action research in education is mainly done by:
o: The teacher, to solve immediate classroom problems
fixed.w: Action research (Stephen Corey in education) is practical research by practitioners to improve their own practice.

fixed.q: The heuristic method of teaching, where the learner acts as a discoverer, was advocated by:
fixed.w: Armstrong's heuristic method puts the student in the position of a discoverer (mainly in science).

fixed.q: The Dalton Plan of individualised instruction was given by:
fixed.w: The Dalton Plan (1920) uses contracts or assignments that students complete at their own pace.

fixed.q: Emotional intelligence was popularised by:
fixed.w: Goleman (1995) popularised EQ: self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy and social skills.

fixed.q: "Gender" as distinct from "sex" refers to:
o: Socially and culturally constructed roles and expectations
fixed.w: Sex is biological; gender is socially constructed, so schools can reinforce or challenge stereotypes.

fixed.q: Showing only boys as engineers and girls as nurses in textbooks is an example of:
fixed.w: Stereotyped portrayals in materials form part of the hidden curriculum.

fixed.q: The "hidden curriculum" means:
o: Values and attitudes learnt implicitly through school culture
The syllabus kept secret from students
fixed.w: Norms learnt from routines, interactions and the school environment rather than the official syllabus.

fixed.q: "Language across the curriculum" means that:
o: Every teacher is responsible for developing students' language in their subject
English must be used in all subjects
Students study several languages each year
fixed.w: Language is central to learning in all subjects, e.g. explaining an algorithm in clear words.

fixed.q: The three-language formula in India was recommended by the:
fixed.w: The formula was proposed in 1961 and endorsed by the Kothari Commission and the 1968 NPE.

fixed.q: Curriculum is broader than syllabus because curriculum includes:
o: All learning experiences, objectives, methods and evaluation
fixed.w: Syllabus is the content outline; curriculum is the whole planned learning experience.

fixed.q: Ralph Tyler's rationale for curriculum development starts with:
fixed.w: Tyler's four questions: objectives, learning experiences, organisation, evaluation.

fixed.q: Using role play or theatre activities to teach concepts (e.g. students acting as packets travelling through a network) is:
fixed.w: Drama and art make abstract ideas concrete and build communication and empathy.

fixed.q: Which approach treats a child's mother tongue as a resource in the classroom?
fixed.w: NCF 2005 and NEP 2020 encourage multilingualism and home-language use.

fixed.q: "Childhood and growing up" as a B.Ed area mainly studies:
o: The development and socio-cultural contexts of children and adolescents
fixed.w: It covers physical, cognitive, social and emotional development and how contexts shape them.

fixed.q: Knowledge that is gained through direct experience and reflection, as in Dewey's view, is called:
fixed.w: Dewey argued that learning comes from experience combined with reflection.

fixed.q: Equity in education means:
o: Giving each learner the support they need to reach equal outcomes
Giving everyone exactly the same resources
fixed.w: Equality = same for all; equity = fair support according to need.

fixed.q: Which of the following comes under socio-emotional development of play?
o: Play provides opportunity for children to demonstrate their abilities and skills
Playing helps to develop memory, and the ability to analyse
By play children learn or develop the ability to keep their mind on task at hand
fixed.w: Showing abilities to others builds confidence and social standing (socio-emotional); memory, analysis, cognition and attention are cognitive benefits.

fixed.q: The ways in which the government has tried to implement the equality that is guaranteed in the constitution is ______. I. through laws II. through government programmes
fixed.w: Equality is implemented both through laws (e.g. RTE, anti-discrimination laws) and through schemes/programmes (e.g. mid-day meal).

fixed.q: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan was launched in _______ year.
fixed.w: SSA, the flagship programme for universal elementary education, was launched in 2001 (2000–01).

fixed.q: Which of the following is an element of effective learning activity? I. Spontaneous involvement II. Challenging
fixed.w: An effective activity draws learners in spontaneously and is challenging enough to stretch them.

fixed.q: The Rishi Valley approach in pedagogy was designed to make the students ______. I. capable of acquiring mastery in learning competencies through both group and individual learning II. understand the importance of physical environment in the classroom
fixed.w: Rishi Valley (multigrade, ladder-of-learning cards) aims at mastery of competencies through group and individual learning.

fixed.q: The objective type items are normally used in most of the tests. Which of the following is the correct example of closed-ended items?
o: Who controls the teachers and students in a school?
In how many ways can you draw a triangle?
Write down as many words adding 'ed' like played, created etc.
fixed.w: A closed-ended item has one fixed correct answer (the principal); the others invite many possible answers (open-ended).

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding formative assessment? I. It is conducted at regular intervals on informal basis. II. It involves self-assessment and peer appraisal. III. It is diagnostic and remedial.
fixed.w: Formative assessment is continuous and informal, uses self/peer assessment, and is diagnostic and remedial — all three.

fixed.q: What is regional art? I. It is the work of a community of unschooled artists keeping alive the traditions specific to its particular culture. II. It reflects the traditional art forms of diverse community groups.
fixed.w: Regional (folk) art is kept alive by community artists and reflects the traditional forms of diverse groups.

fixed.q: The initial Juvenile Justice Act, 1986, defined a boy child below ________ of age and a girl child as below _______ of age, a juvenile.
fixed.w: JJ Act 1986: boys under 16 and girls under 18 were juveniles (the 2000 Act made it 18 for both).

fixed.q: 'Problem related to languages' is one of the hurdles to school-family-community partnerships. Which of the following actions can be taken with respect to this hurdle? I. Set aside a room in the school in which to provide child care during events. II. Have printed materials translated into home languages. III. Help parents set up car pools.
fixed.w: Only translation addresses the language barrier; child care and car pools address time/transport hurdles.

fixed.q: Who among the following is known as Lokhitwadi?
fixed.w: Social reformer Gopal Hari Deshmukh wrote under the pen-name 'Lokhitwadi'.

fixed.q: For preparing a unit plan, which of the following procedure is followed? I. Formation of proper units and sub-units if not prescribed in the syllabus. II. Determination of methods of assessment.
fixed.w: A unit plan divides content into units/sub-units and also decides how learning will be assessed.

fixed.q: David Kolb's model of learning style is based on which type of learning?
fixed.w: Kolb's cycle: concrete experience → reflective observation → abstract conceptualisation → active experimentation (experiential learning).

fixed.q: Inconsistency in the development of different type of conservation is called ______.
fixed.w: Piaget: a child may conserve number before mass or volume — this uneven development is horizontal décalage.

fixed.q: Heuristic method of teaching science was introduced by ______.
fixed.w: H. E. Armstrong advocated the heuristic (learner-as-discoverer) method for science.

fixed.q: Which of the following statement is correct regarding vision of new-born babies? I. Neonates can discriminate between stationary black and white stripe which is 1/8 of an inch wide II. By three months babies can see stripes as narrow as 64th of an inch wide
fixed.w: Newborns resolve ~1/8-inch stripes; visual acuity improves rapidly so by about 3 months they resolve ~1/64-inch stripes.

fixed.q: In the context of Parenting, which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Give and take relationship of parents – Children show same relationship with peer
Clearly communicating parent – Child being less liked
Power assertive parents – Coercive tactics in peer used by child
Parents being harsh – Unattractive social behavior of child
fixed.w: Children carry the give-and-take style they see at home into peer relationships (per the official key).

fixed.q: Broca's area and Wernicke's area are concerned with language. These are the areas of ______. I. right hemisphere of brain. II. left hemisphere of brain.
fixed.w: In most people both Broca's (speech production) and Wernicke's (comprehension) areas are in the left hemisphere.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT a Neo-Freudian Theory of Development? I. Henry Stack Sullivan's Interpersonal Theory II. Erik Erikson Theory of Psycho-social Development
fixed.w: Both Sullivan and Erikson are neo-Freudians, so neither is "not neo-Freudian".

fixed.q: Participation in which of the following activities can enable the community to accept a teacher as one of them? I. Problems of unhygienic conditions. II. Problems of agriculture.
fixed.w: Helping with the community's real problems — hygiene and agriculture alike — makes the teacher part of the community.

fixed.q: Considering the benefits to children with disability, which of the following provisions of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan is correct? I. Stipend for girls with disabilities II. Braille textbooks
fixed.w: SSA inclusive-education provisions include stipends for girls with disabilities and Braille/large-print books.

fixed.q: Reinforcement strengthens the occurrence of the emitted behaviour in the students. Which of the following is the correct example of positive reinforcement?
o: Teacher detaining the student after class hours.
fixed.w: Positive reinforcement adds a pleasant stimulus (good grades) after the desired behaviour.

fixed.q: Which of the following does not come under lower form of writing?
fixed.w: Per the official key, paragraph writing is a higher (composition) form; dictation and guided picture composition are lower forms.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT correct in regard of Piagetian perspective of play?
o: Play is not possible for child without toys
The play is something which transcends both culture and time
The play is something related to nature
fixed.w: Play does not need toys — children play with their bodies, imagination and surroundings.

fixed.q: Which activity do children do to expand their vocabulary? I. Fast mapping II. Sorting
fixed.w: Fast mapping: children attach a new word to a concept after one or two exposures, rapidly growing vocabulary.

fixed.q: In which method of learning by work, students themselves decide objective and prepare plan for an activity?
fixed.w: Kilpatrick's project method: purposing, planning, executing, judging — done by the students.

fixed.q: The 'Kesari' newspaper was published in which language?
fixed.w: Tilak's Kesari was in Marathi (Mahratta was its English counterpart).

fixed.q: According to the Indian Penal Code, an offence is not punishable for a child below _______ of age.
fixed.w: IPC Section 82: nothing is an offence done by a child under 7 years.

fixed.q: Parent and family involvement decreases student's ______. I. Achievement II. Success
fixed.w: Family involvement increases achievement and success; it decreases neither.

fixed.q: Read the following characteristics of one of Piaget's stages of cognitive development: A. Complete generality of thought. B. Development of strong idealism. C. Propositional thinking. Select the correct stage.
fixed.w: Abstract, propositional and idealistic thinking appear in the formal operational stage (11+ years).

fixed.q: Which of the following ailments is NOT caused by obesity?
fixed.w: AIDS is caused by HIV infection; the others are linked to obesity.

fixed.q: When learning is meaning making, then students are the meaning makers. The learning process in this context is ________.
fixed.w: If learners construct meaning, the process is learner/student-centred (constructivist).

fixed.q: Which of the following statement is NOT correctly matched?
o: Performing art - every child should have clear view of board
Child with special need - should be seated near the board
Group work - sitting arrangement should be in clump or clustered
Group discussion - teacher should have eye contact with every child
fixed.w: Performing arts need open space for movement, not a view of the board.

fixed.q: Integrated Child Development Services provides nutritious food for children who are ______.
o: Below age of six years and too young to go to school
fixed.w: ICDS (anganwadis) serves children 0–6 years plus pregnant and lactating mothers.

fixed.q: Which of the following is the activity related to community services?
o: Participating in decoration at the time of events
Collect picture about different musical instrument and dances
Collect information about handicrafts of different place
Explore food habit and living style of the people of different state
fixed.w: Decorating for events is service to the community; the others are information-gathering projects.

fixed.q: Auditory and visual co-ordination system is present in child from ______.
fixed.w: Newborns already turn towards sounds and look in that direction — the co-ordination is present from birth.

fixed.q: All of the given are the methods of Information and Communication Technology-based assessment except ______.
fixed.w: A paper journal uses no ICT.

fixed.q: Which of the following is correctly matched? I. A child calling all four legged animals doggie – under-generalization II. A child using word 'duck' for only his toy duck – over-generalizing
fixed.w: Both are swapped: 'doggie' for all four-legged animals is over-generalisation; 'duck' only for his toy is under-generalisation.

fixed.q: The philosophy of inclusive education was added in District Primary Education Programme (DPEP) in ________ year.
fixed.w: DPEP (1994) added Integrated/Inclusive Education for disabled children in 1997.

fixed.q: The given statement is referring to which type of identity status in adolescents? 'Experimenting and actively searching for alternatives in their struggle to establish their identity.'
fixed.w: Marcia: moratorium = exploring alternatives without commitment yet.

fixed.q: Which of the following stage is used for child cognition development at the age from 2 years to 7 years?
fixed.w: Piaget: sensorimotor 0–2, pre-operational 2–7, concrete 7–11, formal 11+.

fixed.q: The Government of India adopted the National Policy for Empowerment of Women in ______.
fixed.w: The National Policy for the Empowerment of Women was adopted in 2001.

fixed.q: In which of the following approach Pedagogy indicates learning by doing based on engagement of students through different activities? I. Teacher centred approach II. Student centred approach
fixed.w: Activity-based learning by doing is the student-centred approach.

fixed.q: Which of the following approach of Assessment for Learning is the assessment of classmates on the response and performance of the learner?
fixed.w: Classmates assessing each other = peer assessment.

fixed.q: Which of the following language was included through the 71st constitutional amendment (1992) in 8th schedule of the Indian Constitution?
fixed.w: The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; Boro came with the 92nd (2003).

fixed.q: Art education is the area of learning that is based upon which of the following? I. The visual, tangible art II. The performing arts
fixed.w: Art education covers visual arts and performing arts.

fixed.q: In which of the following approach to learning and teaching, both the teacher and the students perform activities strictly confined to the prescribed contents/textbooks in the subject being taught?
fixed.w: Being bound to the prescribed content/textbook is the subject-centred approach.

fixed.q: Piaget divided which of the following domain of development into four stages: the Sensorimotor, Pre-Operational, Concrete Operational and Formal Operational stage?
fixed.w: Piaget's four stages describe cognitive development.

fixed.q: In the types of learning resources, the term ______ denotes a partially three-dimensional, full-size replica or scale model of a landscape typically showing historical events, nature scenes or cityscapes, for purposes of education or entertainment.
fixed.w: A diorama is a 3-D scene model; realia are real objects.

theory.Learning theories:
• Behaviourism: Pavlov (classical conditioning, dogs), Thorndike (trial & error; laws of readiness, exercise, effect; cats), Skinner (operant conditioning, reinforcement; rats/pigeons), Watson.
• Cognitivism/Gestalt: Köhler (insight learning, chimpanzee Sultan).
• Social learning: Bandura (observation, modelling; Bobo doll).
• Constructivism: Piaget (individual), Vygotsky (social; ZPD, scaffolding), Bruner (discovery learning, spiral curriculum; enactive–iconic–symbolic).
• Gardner: multiple intelligences. Goleman: emotional intelligence. Maslow: hierarchy of needs.
theory.Child development & inclusion:
• Piaget stages: sensorimotor 0–2, pre-operational 2–7, concrete operational 7–11, formal operational 11+. Schema, assimilation, accommodation, equilibration.
• Kohlberg: moral development (pre-conventional, conventional, post-conventional). Erikson: psychosocial stages.
• Learning disabilities: dyslexia (reading), dysgraphia (writing), dyscalculia (maths), dyspraxia (motor).
• Inclusive education: all learners in regular classrooms with support (RPwD Act 2016).
theory.Teaching methods & maxims:
• Maxims: known → unknown, simple → complex, concrete → abstract, particular → general, whole → part, easy → difficult.
• Inductive (examples → rule) vs deductive (rule → examples).
• Project method: Kilpatrick (Dewey's learning by doing). Heuristic: Armstrong. Dalton Plan: Helen Parkhurst. Discovery: Bruner.
• CS teaching: demonstration + lab practice, problem solving, pair programming, computational thinking (decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, algorithms).
• Flipped classroom, blended learning, brainstorming (Osborn).
• Edgar Dale's cone: direct experience (concrete) at the base, verbal symbols (abstract) at the top.
theory.Lesson planning & Bloom's taxonomy:
• Bloom 1956 (cognitive): knowledge, comprehension, application, analysis, synthesis, evaluation. Revised 2001 (Anderson & Krathwohl): remember, understand, apply, analyse, evaluate, create.
• Domains: cognitive, affective (Krathwohl: receiving → characterisation), psychomotor (Simpson/Dave).
• Herbart's steps: preparation, presentation, comparison/association, generalisation, application (+ recapitulation).
• Micro-teaching: Stanford 1963 (Dwight Allen). Indian cycle 36 min = teach 6 + feedback 6 + re-plan 12 + re-teach 6 + re-feedback 6. One skill at a time, 5–10 students.
• A lesson plan starts with learning objectives.
theory.Assessment & evaluation:
• Formative (for learning, during) vs summative (of learning, at the end). Diagnostic test → remedial teaching. Placement assessment before instruction.
• Qualities of a test: validity (measures what it should), reliability (consistency), objectivity, usability.
• Norm-referenced (compare with group) vs criterion-referenced (compare with standard).
• Tools: rubrics, portfolios, anecdotal records, checklists, rating scales; a blueprint covers content × objectives × question types.
• CCE: continuous and comprehensive, scholastic + co-scholastic (RTE 2009).
theory.Policies, ICT & CS teaching:
• NEP 2020: 5+3+3+4; coding from Class 6; mother tongue up to Class 5 where possible; 360° holistic progress card.
• RTE Act 2009: ages 6–14, Article 21A (86th Amendment 2002), 25% seats in private unaided schools for EWS/disadvantaged groups (Sec 12(1)(c)), no detention policy amended 2019.
• NCF 2005 (NCERT, Yash Pal): link knowledge to life outside school, learning without burden. NCF-SE 2023 follows NEP.
• ICT platforms: SWAYAM (MOOCs), DIKSHA (teachers, QR textbooks), NROER, e-Pathshala, SWAYAM Prabha (DTH channels).
• CAI (computer-assisted instruction), CMI. Flanders' FIACS: 10 categories. Action research: Stephen Corey.
theory.Gender, language & curriculum:
• Sex = biological; gender = socially constructed. Stereotyping in texts and classroom roles; equality vs equity.
• Hidden curriculum: values learnt implicitly from school culture.
• Language across the curriculum: every teacher is a language teacher; multilingualism as a resource (NCF 2005, NEP 2020); three-language formula (1961, endorsed by Kothari Commission 1964–66).
• Curriculum (all planned learning experiences) vs syllabus (content outline). Tyler's rationale: objectives → experiences → organisation → evaluation.
• Drama and art in education: role play, theatre, art integration for concrete, joyful learning.
• Childhood and growing up: development in socio-cultural contexts.
